Topic: SPI Flash As MSC Backend (Inference)
Statement: REFUTED. No SPI flash IC exists on the board. Two SMD parts near the SoC were photographed and identified: APM4958A (SOP-8, Anpec dual N-channel MOSFET) and an unidentified QFN-10 marked 30502/E09XAA, plausibly a small synchronous buck converter -- neither is a serial flash package. The SPI data lines run directly to the SD card slot with no branch to another SPI device. The original inference rested only on the vendor-default SCSI string "W55FA93 SPI Disk", which CL-USB-REC-117 has since shown to be the Nuvoton MSC library's default string over the SD card, not a hardware description.
Next_Test: Identify the SPI flash part on PCB and compare capacity to 64 MiB.

Why the die carries DWIN branding is undetermined and is recorded as an observation, not explained.

Topic: MT6701 Encoder Uses SoC Pin 117
Statement: The MT6701 encoder connects to SoC pin 117 (GPE[10]/NALE) using a single signal line. Pin 117 multifunction options are only GPIOE[10] / Reserved / NALE / NALE (Design Guide table MF_GPE10) -- there is no PWM or capture function on this pin, so a PWM signal from the MT6701 must be evaluated in software. Merged with CL-SOC-REC-015. The pin-to-encoder mapping comes from continuity measurement on the board, not from a schematic -- no schematic exists for this device. Source: PCB ring-out sessions of 2025-12-19/20 and the In-Circuit column of hardware/N32903U5DN_Pinout.md, whose provenance header states that column derives from visual inspection and continuity measurement at the device. The row still carries the source file's own caveat: its check marks were not uniformly re-verified, and this row is flagged in the file's status column.
Next_Test: Start at VA 0x231F30, the only literal-addressed read of REG_GPIOE_PIN (see CL-HARDWARE-REC-111), and walk callers in Ghidra to the routine that produces the About-screen value 'Encoder OK | <n>'. Topic: Display Rendering Primitives Located -- Fill And Blit Over SPI0
Statement: DECIDED 2026-08-31 (probe B1). MEASURED: two routines drive the panel over SPI0. FUN_0026FD90 writes its r0 argument to REG_SPI0_TX0 and control word 0x45 to REG_SPI0_CNTRL (pool word 0xB8001000 at VA 0x26FDD0, +0xB000 forms the SPI0 window); FUN_0026FDD4 writes r0 to REG_SPI0_TX0 with control word 0x85 (pool word 0xB800C000 at VA 0x26FDF4) and busy-polls bit 0. FUN_0026FD70 clears and sets bit 0x2000 of REG_GPIOD_DOUT (pool word 0xB8001038 at VA 0x26FD8C) around each transfer. A binary scan for BL targets finds 31 call sites of FUN_0026FD90 across APP.bin; the immediates loaded into r0 immediately before them are 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2C (repeatedly, in FUN_0021D0C0 and FUN_0021CAB0), 0x2E once, and the initialisation run 0x11 / 0xB2 / 0xB7 / 0xBB / 0xC3 / 0xC4 / 0xC6 / 0xD0 / 0xE0 / 0xE1 / 0x3A / 0x36 / 0x29 in FUN_0021D1C0 and FUN_0021D77C. 0x3A carries argument 0x55; 0x11 is followed by an immediate 0x78 (120) passed to a delay call. FUN_0021D0C0 sends 0x2A/0x2B/0x2C with computed coordinates and one area value -- a rectangle fill. FUN_0021CAB0 sends the same three, then loops ldrh r0,[r5],#0x2 into FUN_0026FDD4 -- a 16-bit-per-pixel block transfer. DERIVED (not measured): that 0x2A/0x2B/0x2C are CASET/RASET/RAMWR and 0x3A COLMOD=0x55 is RGB565. That naming comes from the ST7789 command table via CL-DISPLAY-REC-002, which found the identical initialisation run in BOOT.bin at +0x52C/+0x5E0. APP.bin carrying the same sequence is an independent second site for the same claim. Bit 13 of REG_GPIOD_DOUT framing each transfer is consistent with a D/C or CS line but is not confirmed by name.
Evidence_E0: 4 [python3 scan of firmware/bin/ZK-INKJET-NANO-APP.bin: decode BL (0xEB) targets to 0x26FD90/0x26FDD4/0x26FD70 and read the preceding mov r0,#imm (0xE3A00xxx); 31/39/5 call sites. Register names from research/findings/n32903_registers.json (generated from vendor/N32901-3_NonOS_BSP SYSLIB/Lib/w55fa93_reg.h). Cross-checked in Ghidra by probe B1, report research/probes/B1-druckpfad/report.md]

Topic: Display Controller Is ST7789V -- Decided
Statement: DECIDED 2026-08-20, open since December. The LCD initialisation sequence sits in BOOT.bin around +0x52C/+0x5E0 and writes, in order: 0x11 SLPOUT, 0xB2 PORCTRL with parameters 0C 0C 00 33 33, 0xB7 GCTRL, 0xBB VCOMS, 0xC3 VRHS, 0xC4 VDVS, 0xC6 FRCTRL2, 0xD0 PWCTRL1, 0xE0 and 0xE1 gamma tables, 0x3A = 0x55 for 16-bit colour, 0x36 = 0xB4 MADCTL, 0x29 DISPON. That command set is the canonical ST7789V bring-up. ILI9341 does not use 0xB2, 0xB7, 0xBB, 0xC4, 0xC6 or 0xD0 in this form -- it uses 0xC0/0xC1 power control, 0xC5/0xC7 VCOM and 0xB1/0xB6. The PORCTRL parameters are the ST7789 datasheet defaults. Cross check: MADCTL 0xB4 has the RGB/BGR bit set, which independently matches the BGR565 channel swap found in the UI decode (finding-0007). The identification came out of triaging an old offset catalogue whose entry called these "T5L register writes" -- T5L is a DWIN display ASIC, a label left over from the period when the SoC was believed to be DWIN rather than Nuvoton.

Topic: USB IRQ Registration
Statement: usbd_irq_setup (0x002AF80C) registers USB IRQ id 0x10 via 0x002A1E88 with r2=0x00109AC4; the dispatcher indexes a handler table at base 0x00000890. The ISR target 0x00109AC4 is not mapped inside APP.bin. KORREKTUR 2026-08-31 (CL-BOOT-REC-113): die genannten Adressen sind Ghidra-Adressen, also Dateioffset + 0x200000. Richtig sind usbd_irq_setup bei VA 0x0010780C (file+0xAF80C), die Registrierung ueber 0x000F9E88 (file+0xA1E88) und der ISR bei 0x00109AC4 (file+0xB1AC4). Der Satz "not mapped inside APP.bin" ist damit erledigt: an file+0xB1AC4 steht ein sauberer Prolog str lr,[sp,#-4]! -- der ISR liegt in APP.bin. Die Handlertabelle bei 0x00000890 liegt in der RW-Region (CL-BOOT-REC-114) und ist dort anfangs null, wird also zur Laufzeit gefuellt.
Next_Test: Den ISR bei file+0xB1AC4 durchgehen und die UDC-Register benennen, die er anfasst: welche Bits von USB_BA (MMIO 0xB1008000) er liest, welche Endpunkte er bedient und wo er die Setup-Pakete ablegt. Danach die Registrierung bei file+0xA1E88 lesen und bestaetigen, dass sie den Slot 0x10 der Tabelle bei 0x890 beschreibt -- IRQ 16 ist UDC_INT laut Design Guide S. 625. Das ist die Voraussetzung dafuer, einen eigenen Endpunkt oder ein eigenes Kommando einzuhaengen, statt das MSC-Fenster zu verschieben.

So the long-standing claim "APP.bin resides at 0x100000 and begins with an ARM IVT" mixed a correct observation with a wrong identification.

Topic: The Junk Is Old ZK Firmware, Not A Foreign Card
Statement: One of the two arguments for this has fallen: the byte-identity of the Vol2 and active APP.bin is explained by the operator restoring recovered files (CL-STORAGE-REC-105), not by device behaviour. What remains is CL-BOOT-REC-104 -- the 3 MB blob at 0x100000 is an earlier firmware of this product line, identified by its own Set A filename strings -- and CL-STORAGE-REC-119, where volume 0 shows a hand-edited vendor font library rather than foreign residue. The ext4 remnants and PNG/JPEG signatures in the gap regions are still unexplained.
Next_Test: Date the blob at 0x100000: compare its Set A filename list and build strings against the Set B list embedded in the current APP.bin at +0x6CFA8. If it is an older generation of the same vendor image, factory reflashing explains it without a foreign owner.

Topic: BMP And CSV On 3:/ Are Outputs, Not Print Input
Statement: The current APP.bin contains "3:/inkjet-ui-%04d%02d%02d %02d%02d%02d %d.bmp" next to "[%s] Print Screen: %s.", and "@3:\inkjet-lite-vadj-sample.csv". Both are files the device writes: a screen capture and a VADJ sampling log. The 2025-11-27 reading of these strings as evidence for a file-based print input path does not hold.

Topic: Firmware Reads Resources From 3:/obds And 0:/user
Statement: Beyond the update filenames, the current APP.bin references 3:/obds/fonts/%s, 3:/obds/res/ZK-INKJET-RES-HW.zkml, 3:/obds/res/GT32L24M0140.spiflash, 3:/obds/res/GT30L24A3W.ZB25VQ32.spiflash, 3:/%d-%s, 0:/user, 0:/user/font and 0:/user/font/%s. These are read paths for user- or vendor-supplied content and are a more promising lever for file-driven control than the BMP/CSV strings were.
Next_Test: Create 0:/user/font/ and 3:/obds/ with test content and observe whether the device picks it up. Locate the corresponding f_open calls in APP.bin to learn what filenames and formats are expected.

Topic: Minimal Image Built For Write-Tracking
Statement: firmware/image/sdcard.minimal.img contains only boot sector, BOOT.bin, APP.bin, the UI frames, the fonts volume and the empty MINI volume; 68.5 percent of it is zero. Omitted on purpose: the previous-generation firmware at 0x100000, the four IBR lookup headers, and the whole 0x24007E00-0x2A61BDFF region with its deleted files, settings, calibration data and ext4 remnants. sha256 32d14c1288dad191a5c73b3dc32703b9e0410c64d6d79f5d587d814f1cff081f, reproducible via tools/scripts/build_clean_image.py.
Next_Test: Flash it, boot, calibrate, set language, print, then re-dump and diff against the image. Every non-zero byte in the diff is a write by the firmware. That retires the remaining speculation about the unmounted region in one experiment. Risk: settings and calibration are gone, and if the device needs anything that was omitted it will not boot -- keep sdcard.work.img as the fallback.

Topic: Minimal Image Boots On The Device
Statement: sdcard.minimal.img was flashed and the printer starts and runs its UI. The image deliberately omits the previous-generation firmware at 0x100000, the four IBR lookup headers (#2 at 0x00179DCC, #3 at 0x0247AA68, #4 at 0x0306CFA8, #5 at 0x03C7BD70) and the entire region 0x24007E00-0x2A61BDFF. None of that is needed to boot. This confirms empirically what CL-BOOT-REC-101, CL-BOOT-REC-104 and CL-STORAGE-REC-104 had argued from the binary alone.

Topic: Settings And Calibration Loss Confirms Their Location
Statement: After booting the minimal image, touch calibration is gone and the language default is unset -- text renders as filled black boxes because no font/language selection is active. The minimal image zeroes exactly the region that holds the settings block (0x28000000) and the calibration slots (0x28800000 + i*0x4D000). Same symptom pattern as the January clean-image test, now reproduced against a reference image whose content is known byte for byte.

Topic: Test Card Is Not The Original Card
Statement: The card now in the reader (/dev/sdc) is 31,719,424,000 bytes, about 29.5 GiB. The original dump sdcard.work.img is 4,026,531,840 bytes. So the minimal image was written to a different, larger card. Two consequences: anything beyond offset 0x2E61BE00 on this card is that card previous content and says nothing about the printer, and the recycled-card question (CL-STORAGE-REC-108) cannot be studied on this medium at all.

Topic: UI Branding Is DCJET / DC-MINI PRINTER
Statement: The running UI shows "DC-MINI PRINTER" in the title bar and "DCJET" as the sample content, while every firmware filename in the update paths is ZK-INKJET-*. The device photographed on 2026-08-19 therefore carries a different brand skin than the firmware naming suggests. Whether this matches the state before the minimal image was flashed is not established -- the operator recalls a different start screen.
Next_Test: Compare against the decoded RAW UI frames in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/artifacts/ui_raw_offsets/ (frame0/1/2). They came out of sdcard.work.img at 0x03800000 and were copied verbatim into the minimal image, so a difference on screen cannot come from those frames and must come from the resource files or from unset configuration.

Topic: Complete Write Footprint Of A Plain Boot
Statement: Measured by flashing sdcard.minimal.img, booting, restarting once, and diffing a raw re-read against the flashed image. The firmware wrote exactly 104 sectors, 53,248 bytes, and nothing else anywhere in the 778 MB: one sector at 0x28000000 (settings), 100 sectors at 0x28800000 + i*0x4D000 for i=0..99 (calibration), one at 0x2A614000 (MBR), and two inside FAT volume 3 (FAT at +0x200, root directory at +0x8200). This closes the question of what is alive in the 102 MB unmounted region: those structures and nothing more. Full trace in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/write_trace/.

Topic: USB-MSC LUN Starts At Raw SD 0x2A614000
Statement: The sector at 0x2A614000 is an MBR: partition type 0x06 (FAT16), start LBA 63, 131,009 sectors = 67,076,608 bytes = 63.97 MiB, signature 0x55AA. 0x2A614000 + 63*512 = 0x2A61BE00, exactly the MINI boot sector, whose own BPB carries hidden_sectors = 63 and total_sectors32 = 131,009. So the drive the host sees over USB begins at 0x2A614000, and 3:/ is the FAT16 partition inside it. That explains the 63-sector offset that made 0x2A61BE00 look like an oddly unaligned volume start. The sector is byte-identical in sdcard.work.img and after boot; the minimal image had omitted it and the firmware recreated it exactly, which is itself the proof that the firmware maintains it.

Topic: Firmware Cleans The MINI Volume At Boot
Statement: On boot the firmware cleared the root directory of volume 3 and freed the corresponding FAT entries. Removed were a "System Volume Information" directory (SYSTEM~1, attribute 0x16, a Windows artefact) and two already-deleted 0xE5 entries for UI-QVGA.bin and ZK-INKJET-UI-*.bin. The FAT went from f8ffffff ffffffff ffff to f8ffffff, i.e. the allocated clusters were released. Anything a host leaves on the MINI drive is therefore subject to a tidy-up at the next boot.
Next_Test: Place a harmless file on the MINI volume, boot, and check whether it survives. That distinguishes a blanket wipe from a selective cleanup and decides whether a file-drop control scheme is viable at all.

Topic: Settings Block Payload Is Larger Than The Documented Struct
Statement: The written settings sector carries non-zero data up to +0x1D7 (471 bytes), while finding-0009 reported a 0x190-byte (400) structure from the sd_raw_write_aligned call. Recognisable content: a rectangle 24/216/216/24 and the value 120 (plausible touch calibration targets on a 320x240 panel), a run of large signed values at +0x54..+0x6C consistent with an affine touch matrix, IEEE-754 doubles 1.8 at +0xA8 and 9.0 at +0xB8 (the latter matches the documented VADJ rail of about 9.09 V), several occurrences of 1000 (0x3E8) matching the value shown on screen, and an ascending 32-bit table from +0x190 to +0x1D6 with a mostly constant step of 0x7E.
Next_Test: Change one setting at a time on the device (language, then a print parameter, then touch calibration), re-dump and diff the single sector each time. Each diff names one field. That decodes the struct without any disassembly.

Topic: Calibration Slot Payload -- Corrected Measurement
Statement: CORRECTION of my own earlier entry: the "127 bytes" figure came from reading only 128 bytes of the sector. The header sector of each entry is used in full: structured data from +0x00 to +0xA7 (18 bytes of 0xFF, then values including the coordinate pattern 32/24, 32/216, 288/216, 288), then 0x55AA repeated as filler from +0xA8 to +0x1FF. The 16-byte figure in finding-0009, taken from a sd_raw_write_aligned(..., 0x10) call, still does not match the observed data. AUFGELOEST 2026-08-19: die 0x10 stammen aus settings_save_calibration_slots @0x265EA8, und diese Funktion speichert nichts, sie LOESCHT. Bei 0x265FE0/0x265FE4 stehen mov r7,#0x4D000 und mov r8,#0x28800000, dann mla r0,r5,r7,r8 in einer Schleife cmp r5,#0x64 ueber 100 Durchlaeufe; der Puffer wird per memset auf 0xFF gesetzt und mit Laenge 0x10 ueber sd_raw_write_aligned geschrieben. Das ist die Initialisierung aller 100 Dokument-Header, und es erklaert die 18 Bytes 0xFF am Anfang von Eintrag 0. Kein Widerspruch mehr, nur eine falsche Benennung.

Topic: Language Index Is settings+0x00, One int32
Statement: Confirmed by a second measurement: switching to German changed exactly one byte in 2 GiB, the int32 at 0x28000000+0x00, from 2 to 13. The prediction made before the test was 13, derived from English = 2 and a row-major 4-per-row grid. sdcard.work.img carries 13 in the same field, so the device was already set to German when it was imaged in September 2025. Decoded ordering: 0 Chinese simplified, 1 Chinese traditional, 2 English, 3 Japanese, 4 Korean, 5 Espanol, 6 Portugues, 7 Francais, 8 Italia, 9 Turk dili, 10 Arabic, 11 Russian, 12 Tieng Viet, 13 Deutsche, 14 Nederland.

Topic: Touch Calibration Occupies Three Field Groups In The Settings Block
Statement: Comparing the original card against the state after recalibration, 25 bytes differ, in three groups: +0x04..+0x14 (values in the 130..900 range, pairwise), +0x2C..+0x3C (same character), and +0x54..+0x68 (large signed values, e.g. 22246118 -> 22351292, -1723531 -> -2148422, consistent with the coefficients and divisor of an affine touch transform). Plus the language field at +0x00 and a flag at +0x180 (1 -> 0). Everything else in the 471-byte payload is unchanged, including the doubles 1.8 and 9.0 and the 1000 values.
Next_Test: Recalibrate once more and diff again. Fields that move a third time are calibration; fields that stay are configuration.

Topic: The 100 Entries Are The Document Store
Statement: Resolved. The Open dialog on the device lists each saved document with a size of 307.94 KB = 315,392 bytes = 0x4D000, exactly the stride of the 100 entries. Saving a document named "Neu-001" wrote entry 1 at 0x2884D000 and its name appears there in plain ASCII at +0x40; entry 0 at 0x28800000 carries "DC-MINI PRINTER" at the same offset. So the store is a 100-slot fixed-size document store for the labels the device prints, and settings+0x180 holds the number of stored documents (1 on the original card, 0 after the minimal image initialised the store, 2 after two documents were created).

Topic: Missing CJK Glyphs Are Not A Font Problem
Statement: The boxes persist after a language has been set, so the earlier lazy-loading explanation is wrong. They cover exactly the entries needing CJK or Hangul coverage: 0, 1 and 3 render as filled bars and 4 (Korean) renders empty, while every Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic and Vietnamese label draws correctly. No file is missing: all 17 font paths that APP.bin references (0:/msyh.ttc, 0:/simsun.ttc, 0:/simhei.ttf, 0:/simkai.ttf, 0:/simfang.ttf, 0:/SIMLI.TTF, 0:/SIMYOU.TTF, the FZ family, DZPMYD, DroidSansFallback, arial, times, OpenSans, Montserrat, SYMBOL) exist on volume 0. 0:/user/font exists and is empty. The remaining explanation is that the list is drawn in one font, the one tied to the active language, whose glyph coverage simply does not include CJK.
Next_Test: Select entry 0 (Chinese simplified) and look at the list again. If the CJK labels then render, the behaviour is single-font rendering and nothing is broken. Deutsche sits at index 13, row 4 column 2, so the way back is a known tile.

Topic: Volume 0 Expects An MBR That Does Not Exist
Statement: The BPB of volume 0 at 0x04000000 declares hidden_sectors = 1, i.e. the volume presents itself as a partition one sector after an MBR at 0x03FFFE00. That sector is all zeros in sdcard.work.img and the firmware never writes it. Volume 3 is the opposite case: its MBR at 0x2A614000 exists and is maintained (CL-USB-REC-105). So only the USB-exposed volume gets a partition table.

Topic: Volume 0 Was Edited By Hand, Not Recycled
Statement: The root directory of volume 0 holds deleted entries alongside the live ones, and the pattern is that of an edited font library rather than a foreign card. Deleted: msimple-handwriting-zh_CN.mod (1,994,504 bytes) whose start cluster 2549 and size are identical to the live ZK-INKJET-RES-HW.zkml that replaced it, ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml (3,934,892 bytes), and a batch of Windows font variants (LeelUIsl, LeelaUIb, NirmalaS, NirmalaB, SEGOEUI, SEGUIBL, SEGOEUIL, SEGUISB, segoeuisl, SEGOEUIB, SEGOEUIZ, SEGOEUII, SEGUIBLI, SEGUILI, SEGUISBI, SEGUISLI). Eleven live fonts are never referenced by APP.bin: the Segoe UI family, Nirmala, LeelawUI, both SourceHan faces, Calibri, Micross, FZSSJW and QisiAaSpot. This looks like a Windows font collection copied on and then pruned by the vendor.

Topic: Volume 0 Directory Is Inconsistent At Cluster 2580
Statement: The live entry LeelawUI.ttf (393,764 bytes) and the deleted entry ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml (3,934,892 bytes) both name start cluster 2580. The data actually stored there is GUI-RES: all 3,934,892 bytes at 0x0E12D000 are byte-identical to firmware/resources/ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml. Reading 0:/LeelawUI.ttf would therefore return the first 393,764 bytes of a different file. Functionally harmless, since APP.bin never references LeelawUI.ttf, but it shows the directory was left in a broken state by whoever edited the volume.

Topic: The Running Firmware Is A Recovered Earlier Generation
Statement: The APP.bin currently at 0x03000000 is not the factory image the device shipped with. The operator recovered bare firmware files from deleted entries on several partitions during partition recovery and put those into service. The running image is an earlier generation that does not yet carry the reseller logo, which is why the splash screen differs from what the documentation describes and why the UI is branded DC-MINI PRINTER / DCJET rather than with the Leon logo. Supersedes the branding hypothesis CL-DISPLAY-REC-105. Consequence for the whole record: every statement about "the firmware" refers to this recovered generation, and comparisons against the vendor original need that qualifier.

Topic: Update Path Confirmed From The Operator Side
Statement: Independently of the code analysis, the operator describes the update path as: firmware files are pushed onto the USB-exposed disk and are copied from there into storage. That is the same path CL-BOOT-REC-103 derived from update_entry_boot_app (0x0026887C) and update_flash_file_to_raw (0x0026CCF8), and it is also why the firmware files were recoverable as bare files at all. Two independent sources, same result.

Topic: Label Text Is Stored As Plain ASCII In The Header Sector
Statement: The whole content of a document sits in the first 512 bytes of its 0x4D000 record. Decoded: magic 0x2022 at +0x00, entry index at +0x04, a counter at +0x08, two timestamps as six int32 each (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) at +0x10 and +0x28 which match the dialog exactly (2005-08-30 21:01:32 and 21:03:24, the RTC was never set), the document name as NUL-terminated ASCII at +0x40, and the text content as NUL-terminated ASCII at +0x178 -- "DCJET" in the saved sample. Between those, a block at +0x144..+0x168 holding 1, ffffff00, 405, 405, 1, 25, which looks like the descriptor of a single text object. Full layout in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/document_store.md.

Topic: Only Five Sectors Per Document Are Written, Four Of Them Garbage
Statement: Saving a document writes exactly five sectors of its record: +0x00, +0x200, +0x600, +0x6600 and +0x4CE00. The last four are byte-identical between the two documents and contain scattered values including 04 10 96 e5 0b 00 a0 e1 at +0x4CFC0, which are ARM instruction words (ldr r1,[r6,#4]; mov r0,r11). That is residual RAM written along, not document data -- the same values also sit in the unused area of entry 0 on the original card. The record is fixed-size regardless of content.

Topic: Programmatic Labelling Needs One Sector, No Firmware Change
Statement: Given CL-STORAGE-REC-121 and -122, creating a label on the device reduces to writing one 512-byte sector at 0x28800000 + i*0x4D000 and incrementing settings+0x180. No firmware patch, no USB-CDC, no Ghidra. This makes the original project goal -- labelling lithium cells automatically -- reachable on the storage path instead of the code path. BESTAETIGT durch CL-STORAGE-REC-125: das Verfahren funktioniert am Geraet.

Topic: Main Screen #1 Is The Print Count, The Green Bar The Ink Estimate
Statement: Operator correction to my earlier reading: the "#1" field on the main screen is the number of prints, and the green bar is the computed ink level of the cartridge. I had speculated it was a document or job selector, which it is not -- documents are chosen through the Open dialog.

Topic: Host-To-Raw-SD Mapping Located In Code
Statement: The constant 0x2A614000 (the USB LUN base) appears in the literal pool at VA 0x21CAAC, used by two functions: usb_lun_write_blocks (0x21CA60) and usb_lun_read_blocks (0x21C998), now renamed. write does dst = 0x2A614000 + (hostLBA<<9) and calls sd_fmi_block_io (0x294584); read is the mirror. So the PC-to-device write channel exists in the firmware already: a host sector X written over USB-MSC lands at raw SD 0x2A614000 + X*512. The callers are the MSC SCSI layer (msc_scsi_dispatch_278bb0 at 0x278BB0, plus FUN_0022CDE4 and FUN_002BAD5C). This is the read/write half of the "slave" path and needs no patch.

Topic: Document Store Is Not Reachable Through The USB LUN -- Confirmed, And The Reader Runs The Other Way
Statement: The USB-exposed disk begins at 0x2A614000 and its FAT16 partition (3:/) runs from 0x2A61BE00. The document store sits at 0x28800000, which is BELOW the LUN base, so a host writing to the MINI drive cannot reach the store directly over USB -- the two live in different regions of the raw card. Writing a label from the PC therefore is not "drop a file on the MINI drive"; it needs either (a) direct raw SD access with the card in a reader, or (b) a firmware path that copies from 3:/ into the store, which is exactly what the update chain does for firmware files (CL-BOOT-REC-103/107). Whether a comparable copy path exists for documents is the open question for the slave goal. DECIDED 2026-08-31 (probe B2), negative. The reader exists and is FUN_00265B08: it walks all 100 slots, forms the address as 0x28800000 + index * 0x4D000 via mla, reads 16 header bytes through the raw primitive FUN_00232434 (a raw card address, not a file handle), checks the magic 0x2022, reads the slot and writes it out with fopen("3:/%d-%s","wb+"). Direction is store -> host, i.e. an export, not an import. The target test is negative for all eight address-forming sites found: base and stride are parameters of the scan routine, not one fixed pair, and 100 * 0x4D000 from 0x28800000 ends to the byte at 0x2A614000 -- the LUN base itself. No slot lies at or above it, so no slot is USB-writable and there is no patch-free host-to-store bridge along this path. The self-running string candidates were checked too: the resource and font loaders read from 3:/ but write nothing into the store, and inkjet-lite-vadj-sample.csv is opened "wb" and written, not read. This leaves the eight-byte window patch (CL-USB-REC-119) as the route for the transport half of the goal.
Evidence_E0: 3 +4 [research/probes/B2-usb-bruecke/report.md: four-mode search for magic 0x2022 and for base/stride, disassemble_at on 0x265B08 and 0x232434, geometry computed, string-to-code cross reference for the self-running candidates]

Topic: Application Firmware Does Not Expose MSC By Itself
Statement: Decided by the operator, who has established this before and confirmed it today: the printer firmware does NOT enumerate as mass storage on its own. It requires the menu action Setup -> USB. The strings "USB aktualisieren ...", "Refresh USB...", "Waiting for connection..." and "Device is connected!" belong to that handler. The enumeration seen without a menu press was the boot ROM (idProduct 9396, WPMUSB) with the SD card removed, not the firmware. Consequence for any PC-driven scheme that goes through the application firmware: the channel is not autonomous, and forcing that flag is the first thing such a patch has to do.

Topic: Boot Hold-Key Is The Update Trigger, Not The MSC Switch
Statement: The boot-time hold-key check arms maybe_update_from_udisk at 0x0026887C, i.e. it starts a firmware update scan of 3:/. It does not toggle USB visibility; the two mechanisms were conflated in the older documentation. Which physical key it is has been an open question since finding-0013 and is still unanswered. STARKER KANDIDAT 2026-08-19: boot_init @0x25B0C4 referenziert ueber 0x25B16C/0x25B1AC den String "Please release the print key!" @0x25B25C und liest dabei GPIO ueber 0x26FBF8/0x26FC20. Der beim Booten gehaltene Taster ist damit sehr wahrscheinlich die DRUCK-Taste.
Next_Test: Beim Einschalten die Drucktaste gedrueckt halten und beobachten, ob der Update-Scan von 3:/ anlaeuft.

Topic: LUN Geometry Confirmed From The Host Side
Statement: The host reports the exposed disk as 131072 logical blocks of 512 bytes = 64.0 MiB with a single partition sdf1. The MBR we read at raw SD 0x2A614000 declares partition start LBA 63 and 131009 sectors, and 63 + 131009 = 131072 exactly. So the disk the host sees begins at 0x2A614000 and the mapping host LBA X -> raw SD 0x2A614000 + X*512 is confirmed from both ends: from the card image, from the firmware code (usb_lun_write_blocks at 0x21CA60), and now from the host. Identity as documented: 0416:0093, bcdDevice 11.00, "USB MSC" / nuvoTon / 00000055FA93, SCSI inquiry "W55FA93 SPI Disk".

Topic: IBR USB Boot Mode Confirmed On The Host
Statement: Without an SD card the SoC enumerates from its internal boot ROM: idVendor 0416, idProduct 9396 (the application firmware uses 0093), bcdDevice 1.00, Product WPMUSB, Manufacturer NUVOTON, SerialNumber NUVOTON, SCSI inquiry "W55FA93 USB DEV. Device", and a fabricated capacity of 2,151,546,881 blocks = 1.00 TiB. The stale Read(10) failure at sector 2,151,546,752 in the same log is the kernel probing the end of that fake disk, not a real access. This was claimed from string analysis in December 2025 and is now confirmed at the host.

Topic: Boot ROM Code Upload -- Value Is Recovery, Not Control
Statement: The IBR mass-storage mode is the vendor programming path. vendor/N32905_NonOS_Tool/TurboWriter/ holds the "TurboWriter Tool User Guide.pdf" and FA93_musb.bin (187,416 bytes), which is the loader stub the tool pushes into the chip over exactly this channel; FA93_musb_FullSpeed.bin is the full-speed variant. The device side is in the BSP as source: SDWRITER/Src/Writer.c, SPIWRITER/Src/Writer.c, NANDWRITER/Src/Writer.c, plus UDC/lib/w55fa93_MSC_* for the USB layer. For the goal of driving the printer from the PC this outranks patching APP.bin: it runs code the host supplies, needs no SD card, touches no stored firmware, and a power cycle with the card inserted restores normal operation. STRATEGIE-KORREKTUR 2026-08-19: dieser Pfad ist NICHT der Hauptweg zum Ziel. Wer eigenen Code auf dem Chip ausfuehrt, muss den Druckkopf selbst ansteuern -- Pulsbreiten, HA/HP-Timing, VADJ. Genau dieses Wissen ist am Geraet nicht rekonstruierbar und soll auch nicht rekonstruiert werden. Der IBR-Pfad fuehrt damit zwangslaeufig zu "Firmware neu schreiben", was ausdrueckliches Nichtziel ist. Sein bleibender Wert ist die Wiederherstellung: ein gebricktes Geraet laesst sich ohne Kartenleser zurueckholen.
Next_Test: Nur bei Bedarf: usbmon-Mitschnitt waehrend TurboWriter laeuft, um das Stage-1-Protokoll zu dokumentieren. Als Versicherung sinnvoll, nicht als naechster Schritt.

Topic: Uploaded Code Runs In RAM -- Objection Answered
Statement: Answered in the vendor documentation. The TurboWriter guide states the tool "is connected to Turbo writer firmware which loaded from PC to N329/N9H2X series by USB boot" -- the boot ROM receives a binary over USB and executes it. FA93_musb.bin confirms it structurally: header magic 0x2054564E ("NVT ") followed by execution address, size and version, then from offset 0x20 a genuine ARM vector table (eight times E59FF018 = LDR PC,[PC+0x18], and EAFFFFFE = B . as the abort stub). For the N329x3 variant the header carries execution address 0x00400000 and size 0x2DC08 = 187,400 bytes, which lies inside the 8 MB DDR. So the SD card is the boot medium, not a mandatory waypoint: writing to the card is what the vendor payload does, not what the channel requires. Chapter 1.3 of the guide goes further and documents a "Download and run" function that loads an arbitrary host binary to a chosen buffer address and executes it.

Topic: IBR Image Header Format
Statement: Images for the boot ROM carry a 32-byte header: magic 0x2054564E ("NVT "), then execution address, image size and a version field; the ARM code begins at offset 0x20. Observed values: N329x3 variant 0x00400000 / 187,400 bytes, N329x1 variant 0x00150000 / 187,308 bytes. The guide text names 0x000F00000 generically, which contradicts both binaries and looks like a typo -- the per-chip value in the header is authoritative. DDR initialisation appears to be done by the boot ROM on this family: the guide notes DRAM init was REMOVED from the IBR for N3292X/N9H26K5 and that users must add it there, an exception that is not stated for N3290X.

Topic: Stage-1 Wire Protocol Is Undocumented But Capturable
Statement: The byte-level handshake the boot ROM uses to receive and start the image is not in any source available here. The BSP writer sources only implement the ordinary MSC SCSI set (0x1A, 0x1B, 0x28, 0x2A, 0x3F) of the later stage; the IBR side exists only as the closed TurboWriter.exe and the binary blobs. Reverse-engineering it from scratch is unnecessary: run the vendor tool once and record what it sends.
Next_Test: modprobe usbmon, start a capture on the bus, let TurboWriter (Windows or Wine) perform "Download and run" with FA93_musb.bin, and read the CBWs out of the capture. That converts the undocumented protocol into a documented one in one afternoon and yields a Python reimplementation for Linux. Fallback if the tool will not run: replay the capture with sg_raw.

Topic: The Existing Firmware Is The Asset, Not The Obstacle
Statement: Strategic decision. The goal is a printer driven from the PC, not a replacement firmware. The vendor firmware already holds the one thing that cannot be recovered by measurement: how to fire the printhead -- pulse widths, HA/HP sequencing, VADJ control. Any route that runs own code on the bare chip inherits the obligation to reproduce all of it. A patch does not: it has to understand interfaces, not physics, and calls the routine that already knows the timing. The question therefore is not "how do I execute my own code" but "where is the print entry point and what is the smallest thing that can call it". I had drifted toward the most powerful primitive instead of the cheapest path; this row exists so that drift is on record.

Topic: Document Slot Access Routines Located
Statement: Base and stride appear as MOV immediates, not as pool words: mov r7,#0x4D000 and mov r8,#0x28800000 at 0x265FE0/0x265FE4, address formed by mla r0,index,stride,base. FUN_0028A1D0 writes a single slot header generically, FUN_0028A248 scans all 100 and validates against the magic 0x2022 (pool word at 0x28A3D8) and the timestamp fields -- that is the directory scan, called from ui_main_loop via 0x25F228. FUN_0028A3DC checks the magic on an already loaded record. Proposed names: document_slots_erase_all_headers (0x265EA8), docslot_write_header_generic (0x28A1D0), docslot_scan_find_valid (0x28A248), docslot_check_magic_2022 (0x28A3DC). Not isolated: the routine that writes a complete document including name at +0x40 and text at +0x178.
Next_Test: Find the full-document writer: look for callers of FUN_0028A1D0 with a length greater than 0x10, or set a different document name on the device and diff the single header sector to see which code path produced it.

Topic: Two Constant Search Modes Are Needed, Not One
Statement: Companion to CL-TOOL-REC-101. There the trap was that Ghidra scalar search misses constant-pool words, so I switched to byte searching the file. That failed here for the opposite reason: 0x28800000 and 0x4D000 are encodable as ARM immediates and live inside MOV instructions, so they appear nowhere as data words -- my byte search returned zero hits for both while the constants sit plainly in the code. Neither method alone is sufficient. A negative result from one search mode says nothing until the other has been run.

Topic: UI Strings Are Reached Through An Indexed Table
Statement: The strings "Print", "Printing...", "Drucken..." at 0x3F0500, 0x3F2B68 and 0x3FA7A8 have zero direct cross-references. They are addressed through an indexed string table rather than by ADR, which is why no UI handler can be found by following a string. This is the structural obstacle to locating the print trigger, and it blocks every other UI-level question in the same way. Solving it once unlocks all of them.
Next_Test: Find the string table: locate the array of pointers into the 0x3Fxxxx region and the function that indexes it. Then map string index to handler and the print entry point falls out.

Topic: The Firmware Embeds Zint, The Open Source Barcode Library
Statement: 127 distinct error strings in Zint's exact numbered format are present, verbatim: "206: Symbology out of range, using Code 128", "217: Symbology does not support ECI switching", "219: NULL characters not permitted in GS1 mode", "228: Invalid rotation angle", "232: Incomplete escape character in input data", "289: UPCA input wrong length" and so on. The library name itself was stripped, but the message catalogue is unmistakable. Consequence: the entire barcode engine is open source and documented -- no reverse engineering needed for that part. And unlike the UI strings, these DO have cross-references, which makes them a way into the code: each numbered message is emitted by one known Zint function, so ZBarcode_Encode and its caller can be identified by matching the message catalogue against the upstream sources. AMENDED 2026-08-31: the last sentence of this row assumed that the caller of the encoder sits one step from the print path. CL-FIRMWARE-REC-103 has since shown that this caller (FUN_002302EC) emits CASET/RASET/RAMWR to the ST7789 panel via CL-DISPLAY-REC-004, i.e. it renders the preview. The way into the code through the message catalogue stands unchanged; only the expectation of where it comes out is withdrawn. Confidence lowered from 1.00 to 0.95 on 2026-08-31: the row is O2 and the string catalogue is the whole of its evidence, so it sits at the ceiling of that tier, not above it.
Next_Test: Use the message catalogue for what it is good for now: recovering the zint_symbol structure. Match the numbered messages to their emitting functions in the Zint sources, and from the field offsets those functions touch, reconstruct the layout of the symbol struct that FUN_002302EC fills -- in particular where the encoded bitmap, its row count and its width live. Then search for every other reader of that buffer: whoever rasterises for the print head must consume the same structure, and that reader is the target of CL-FIRMWARE-REC-107. Run both a literal and a scalar search for the struct base per Rule 6.

Topic: Supported Barcode Symbologies
Statement: An 8-byte-aligned run in the string pool at 0x3F03C8 lists: EAN13, ITF14, INT25, PDF417, CODE128, EAN128, EAN8, CODE39, UPCA, UPCE, QRCODE, DATAMATRIX. So the device can print 2D codes. For labelling lithium cells with serial numbers, DATAMATRIX, QRCODE and CODE128 are the relevant ones and they are already available without any modification.

Topic: The Vertical Byte Runs Are Glyph Names, Not UI Text
Statement: The region at 0x3630AC that reads like UTF-16 -- 61 00 62 00 63 00 ... -- is not UTF-16 at all. It is a run of NUL-terminated single-character strings inside a PostScript/AFM glyph name table: "score", "quoteleft", then "a", "b", "c" through "z", then "bracketleft", "braceleft". A font engine artefact, unrelated to the UI. Recorded so it is not chased again.

Topic: Zint Call Chain Located -- And It Ends At The Display, Not At The Print Head
Statement: FUN_0022647C (0x22647C-0x22714B) is the symbology dispatch: it holds all six "Symbology out of range, using Code 128" strings and calls the per-symbology encoders, among them the QR encoder at 0x27406C (which carries "566: Error correction level H not available") and the UPC/EAN block at 0x24C8D8/0x24C950, plus 0x257378, 0x25917C, 0x287A2C, 0x28A53C, 0x2AFB50, 0x2B3770, 0x2B3A94. FUN_0022714C wraps it, and FUN_002302EC (0x2302EC-0x230A5F, 23 callees) calls that wrapper -- shape and size match Zint library.c around ZBarcode_Encode_Segs. Two independent chains reach it from ui_main_loop: ui_main_loop(0x26A8B4, 0x26BB7C) -> FUN_002C31C8 -> FUN_002C2098 -> FUN_002302EC, and ui_main_loop(0x26B86C) -> FUN_0025B338 -> FUN_002C3554 -> FUN_002302EC. The exported names are stripped; identification rests on the message catalogue. The embedded Zint predates current master -- the string "using Code 128" no longer exists upstream. CLOSED 2026-08-31 (probe B1). The three callees of FUN_002302EC that were still unexamined do NOT lead into rasterisation or print output. FUN_002BAD40 (24 bytes) is a trampoline into FUN_0021D0C0, and FUN_002BAD5C reaches FUN_0021CAB0; both are the SPI0 display primitives of CL-DISPLAY-REC-004 (fill and 16-bit block transfer). Neither is barcode-specific: they have 40 and 22 inbound xrefs spread across the whole UI, of which exactly one each comes from FUN_002302EC (0x23034C and 0x230A28). FUN_002A10C8 allocates a working buffer, fills it and frees it again inside the same function, and has a second caller FUN_0026EDDC which references ".jpg", ".png" and ".bmp" -- image handling, not encoding. No callee carries a numbered Zint error string. POSITIVE CONTROL for this negative finding: the same callee traversal did resolve a complete output path (SPI0 command/data senders, register names from the BSP header), so the method demonstrably finds output paths where they exist. CONSEQUENCE: a function that both encodes and emits CASET/RAMWR is not ZBarcode_Encode_Segs; FUN_002302EC is better read as a render routine containing or calling the encoder, and the library.c mapping in the first half of this row is weakened accordingly. Where the raster data for the print head is produced is now an open question in its own right -- see CL-FIRMWARE-REC-107.
